THE ILLUSION OF THE TELEOLOGICAL ESCALATOR
History is frequently taught as a moral success story-a relay race where the "torch of liberty" is passed linearly.
This teleology is empirically false. It erases the vast, interconnected networks of the "people without history"
who actively shaped, funded, and fueled the modern world.

The world in 1400: A continuous tapestry of exchange
Long before European hegemony, the globe was densely woven with contentious political systems and
long-distance trade. Archipelagos of agricultural wealth were linked by vast corridors of commerce,
mobilizing human labor and extracting surpluses across staggering distances.

The Pastoral Corridor
A continuous dry belt of steppe and desert.
Pastoral nomads acted as a high-speed
centrifugal highway, patrolling routes,
extracting protection rents, and
massing cavalry.
The Agricultural Archipelagos
Spotty, compartmentalized zones of arable land.
Rulers focused inward on intensive cultivation
and tax extraction, repeatedly falling prey to
the mobile military supremacy of the steppe.

The engine of connection: Modes of Production
To understand this interconnected tapestry, geography and trade are not enough. We must examine the
underlying political-economic frameworks-the Modes of Production- that dictate how human labor is mobilized,
how nature is transformed, and who extracts the surplus.

The Tributary Mode: The logic of 1400
In 1400, the world was dominated by the Tributary Mode. The primary producer possessed
their own tools and land, but surplus was extracted through political or military coercion
("other than economic pressure").

The Continuum of Power
This mode oscillates based on the strength of the state. When the
center is strong, it extracts tribute directly. When the center is weak, local
overlords intercept the wealth, resulting in fragmented local domains.

The Capitalist Disruption: Commodifying the human capacity to work
Capitalism is not just trade or "mercantile wealth." It is a revolutionary transformation of production itself.
Wealth only becomes Capital when it relentlessly drives technological innovation to maximize surplus.

Synthesis: The hijacking of the tapestry
Capitalism did not invent global interconnectedness. It was a hyper-extractive new mode of production that hijacked,
repurposed, and fed upon the vast, pre-existing networks of the Tributary and Kin-ordered worlds. Capital rewired
the infrastructure to compel labor and extract surplus on an industrial scale

The architects of the modern world
The populations frequently dismissed by historians as isolated, pristine, or primitive were, in fact,
active participants in a deeply interconnected global manifold.
There are no "people without history." They were the foundational scaffolding of the modern global
economy, suffering the impact of capitalist expansion while acting as its indispensable agents.
